title: State Department seeks mid-career hires to join its ranks after widespread layoffs
summary: The Lateral Entry Pilot Program marks State’s latest step to rebuild its workforce. Employees it laid off last year haven’t had much luck in the hiring process.

title: Ex-government tech leaders pitch new vision for America.gov
summary: The proposal goes beyond a single online portal, calling for changes to the underlying systems that determine eligibility and enroll people in federal and state benefit programs.

title: The census shows what government does well — and what political interference could break, author argues
summary: A university researcher who embedded in the Census Bureau ahead of the 2020 national headcount warns in a new book that President Donald Trump’s federal workforce reforms, paired with decades of “Jenga politics,” could put the next census at risk.

title: OPM is ending a promotion rule, but agencies still have work to do
summary: COMMENTARY | A former federal HR chief argues that managers need to pay closer attention to who gets the assignments and experience that make employees competitive for promotion.

title: More Medicare questions? Here’s what federal retirees need to know
summary: Got questions about HSA contributions, TRICARE For Life or keeping FEHB or PSHB when you enroll in Medicare? Here are answers to help you navigate the details of your federal health benefits.

title: DHS personnel leak exposes contact details and sensitive job information
summary: A group calling itself the Department of Peace claimed responsibility for obtaining records on more than 41,000 employees and contractors, citing opposition to immigration enforcement.

title: USDA sends more relocation notices, seemingly in violation of court order
summary: A court-ordered stay prohibits USDA from issuing or enforcing "any other notice or directive of reassignment or relocation in whole or in part."

title: Underused federal office data incomplete but improving
summary: The Government Accountability Office wrote that gaps in USE IT Act data are giving agencies an incomplete understanding of the state of their real estate footprint.

title: Mediation agency finalizes rule allowing denial of arbitrator requests
summary: Union officials said that though the final rule is an improvement over the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service’s initial plan, it still improperly usurps arbitrators’ authority.

title: FEC takes down electronic filing platform after attempted hack
summary: The commission holds no role in administering U.S. elections, meaning any impacts to its systems will not affect voting in the upcoming midterms.

title: DHS secretary plans post-election security review
summary: Markwayne Mullin told CISA employees he wants to assess election systems after the vote, as the agency faces scrutiny over cuts to its support for states.

title: ‘Life-and-death implications’: Former IG warns ICE’s detention oversight is masking unsafe conditions
summary: An analysis by the Project on Government Oversight found that the number of immigration detention facilities receiving a “superior” rating increased at the same time as the number of individuals dying in Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody also surged.

title: OPM touts ‘hire-palooza’ event for early-career employees
summary: A good government group criticized the Office of Personnel Management for providing limited information about the virtual hiring fair, which is restricted to individuals who are already in the federal hiring process.

title: Federal workforce cuts linked to lower satisfaction scores across government services
summary: An annual scorecard that tracks citizen satisfaction in public-facing services shows the federal government’s first overall decline in five years.

title: Federal agencies have until Thursday to fix website security flaws
summary: The vulnerabilities could let hackers take control of government web servers without a password, but the extent of successful attacks remains unclear.

title: Judge: ‘Article II’ firings violate separation of powers, civil service law
summary: U.S. District Judge Jesse Furman said adopting the Trump administration’s argument that the Civil Service Reform Act usurps presidential power would “unsettle the very equilibrium of this nation’s constitutional system.”

title: IRS says it needs top performers, even if they don’t all get the performance ratings they deserve
summary: An IRS division that reassigned employees to different parts of the agency to address backlogs is warning staff against “deliberately choosing mediocrity” in their day-to-day work if they get lower performance ratings this year.

title: SSA ‘corrects’ millions of Social Security Number database files
summary: The agency says the data cleaning is part of its commitment to prevent fraud, but at least one group is raising concerns about the work.

title: SBA is moving field offices away from major cities, union says
summary: The Small Business Administration previously said that it would relocate offices out of certain cities due to disagreements about federal immigration enforcement.

title: NOAA wants better forecasts. First, it needs to rethink how it handles weather data
summary: Moving computing operations to the cloud could give forecasters more flexibility, but the agency is still working through how to make the transition.

title: Navy’s tech playbook serves as a ‘toolkit’ for the rest of government
summary: The U.S. Navy dramatically upped its use of pilot tech programs, shuttered old technology systems and moved into the modern tech arena — and it is sharing its lessons learned along the way.

title: USDA, undeterred by judge’s stay, moves ‘full-bore ahead’ with reorganization steps
summary: The Agriculture Department is still carrying out reorganization activities not explicitly barred by a judge’s stay.

title: Bureau of Prisons seeks another shot at ending union contracts
summary: One union local president said he is still routinely denied official time, has meeting requests ignored, and that his prison has failed to reinstitute compressed work schedules.

title: The legal fight over the public service student loan forgiveness overhaul may be over
summary: Two different federal judges in June ruled that the Education Department’s changes to the program were unlawful. On Wednesday, the Trump administration dropped its appeals.
